articles.title: Second Israel game won't be a friendly - Hallgrimsson
articles.summary: Republic of Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson admits Sunday's second game against Israel is "not going to be a friendly" following comments from the latter's camp after last week's match in Hungary.
body: Having faced calls to boycott the Nations League fixtures because of the ongoing Israel-Gaza war, the Republic of Ireland did not engage in pre-match formalities and bowed their heads during the Israeli national anthem in Debrecen.
After a 3-0 win for the Republic of Ireland, Israel captain Manor Solomon said "we have a country 10 times better than theirs".

Following Thursday's 2-2 draw with Austria in Dublin, Hallgrimsson was asked if those comments will make for a tense encounter with Israel in Sunday's behind-closed-doors game in the Serbian town of Backla Topola.
"I guess so it's not going to be a friendly," said Hallgrimsson.

articles.title: India beat arch-rivals Pakistan in Japan to claim Asian Games cricket gold
articles.summary: India 211-6; Pakistan 192-6 in Twenty20 cricket final. Captains refuse traditional pre-match handshakes. India beat their fierce rivals Pakistan by 19 runs to complete a golden double in the Asian Games cricket after a pulsating final in front of a small but raucous crowd in Nagoya, Japan.
body: The neighbouring countries only meet in international tournaments and on neutral ground because of political tensions and the captains refused the normal handshakes before the match on Saturday. Afterwards, the jubilant India players paraded their national flag around the ground. The clash on a converted baseball field in Japan was new ground for even these rivals and their hundreds of millions of fans who were watching back home on television.

After India chose to bat, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi made clear his intention with back-to-back sixes in a second over from Saad Masood that cost 24 runs. But the 15-year-old batting sensation fell four balls later for 15. His opening partner, Abhishek Sharma, reached his fifty off 20 balls to an ovation from fans that had brought a touch of South Asia cricket fever to the Korogi Park Athletic Stadium.

India were aided by some sloppy Pakistan fielding that saw Abhishek dropped twice. He should also have been run out on 46 when Ahmed Daniyal’s throw missed both stumps and the wicketkeeper with Abhishek stranded.

articles.title: Thrown in with Giggs and Beckham: how Manchester United tried to get Billy Kenny
articles.summary: Former Everton midfielder, known as the ‘Goodison Gazza’, recalls being made to feel special by Alex Ferguson in this autobiography extract. “So this is the scouser ya been goin’ on aboot then …” My face turned Manchester United red.
body: Brian Kidd had just introduced me to the Man United first team by silencing the room to draw attention to my presence. “Lads, this is Billy from up the road,” he said. I was still starstruck from seeing all these famous faces as my chauffeur for the day, Eric Harrison, pulled up in the car park at The Cliff a few minutes earlier. Paul McGrath. Mark Hughes. Bryan Robson. Kevin Moran. Norman Whiteside. I ticked them all off in my head. Thank fuck I was developing an ear for everyday Glaswegian because after a bit of piss-taking from the first-teamers about being a scouser, I found myself standing in an office at the end of a short and narrow corridor, shaking hands with another one.

articles.title: Too quiet for too long, can McGinn recapture best for Scotland?
articles.summary: Fifth in the all-time scoring chart for Scotland and closing in on 100 caps, John McGinn could do with finding his best stuff again, writes Tom English.
body: In Skopje these past few days it's been difficult to figure out the most devout people - the local followers of the city's most sacred daughter, Mother Teresa, or the arriving Scots and their most cherished son, Saint John McGinn.

Faith in the blessed one is absolute (and the same goes for Teresa). Raise a critical note and you could be shot down in flames. Point out that McGinn's talismanic excellence has been on the wane in international football for a little while now and you're liable to reap a whirlwind.
This is a weekend when Andy Robertson wins his 100th cap, but McGinn isn't far behind.
After Saturday night he'll be on 92, third on the all-time appearance list while currently sitting in fifth in the all-time scoring chart, one behind the immortal Lawrie Reilly.

articles.title: India beat Pakistan to take Asian Games gold
articles.summary: Abhishek Sharma and Tilak Varma set India on their way to victory as they beat Pakistan to win gold at the Asian Games.
body: Having opted to bat first in Nagoya, India racked up a commanding 211-6 with Abhishek smashing seven sixes as he made 61 from 28 balls at the top of the order.
A stunning start helped the defending champions reach 81-2 at the end of the powerplay as Abhishek dominated the bowling before falling in the eighth over.
But the runs kept coming and Tilak's unbeaten 51 from 22, which featured three fours and four sixes, kept the momentum going until the end of innings.
Pakistan were soon in trouble in the chase, slipping to 39-3 and, despite a superb knock of 96 from Hasan Nawaz, they came up well short.

articles.title: Why beating Denmark matters to Wales' Euro 2028 hopes
articles.summary: Avoiding finishing bottom of their Nations League group is a major aim for Wales following a win over Erling Haaland's Norway.
body: There has not been much time for Craig Bellamy and Wales to enjoy their Nations League win over Norway.
After taking one Scandinavian scalp, the task is to claim another as Denmark come to Cardiff City Stadium on Sunday (19:45 BST).
Victory would mean recording back-to-back wins over higher-ranked nations for the first time in more than a decade.
It also offers an opportunity to take a huge step towards securing their top-tier Nations League status – and significantly boost their Euro 2028 qualification hopes.

articles.title: Former Real Madrid assistant backs Jose Mourinho’s appointment: ‘Ideal coach at this moment’
articles.summary: Jose Mourinho is Real Madrid’s desperate attempt to bring the team back on track after two trophy-less seasons. Last year, the team failed to win any silverware and saw two young managers arrive with radical ideas and eventually fail to bring out success.
body: The year before that, it was Carlo Ancelotti who failed to bring home silverware and eventually left the club to take up a role in the Brazilian national team.
Carlo Ancelotti’s son Davide Ancelotti recently spoke out in a detailed conversation with AS, where he backed Jose Mourinho’s appointment and explained the rationale behind the club’s decision.
“Yes. Recent Madrid history shows why Mourinho is the ideal coach at this moment,” he began, backing the appointment.

“He is in love with Madrid and has an enormous amount of motivation. It’s something I experienced with my father. At this stage of their careers, having this opportunity is like getting to live it all over again,” he added.

articles.title: Verstappen beats Hamilton to pole in Malaysia
articles.summary: Max Verstappen claimed Red Bull's first pole position of the season as he beat Lewis Hamilton in qualifying for the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.
body: Verstappen and Hamilton will share the front row in Sunday's race at 8am (build-up from 6.30am), live on Sky Sports F1 and Main Event, for the first time since Hungary 2023 after the Red Bull driver delivered a dominant qualifying performance.
The Dutchman topped each segment of qualifying and set two laps good enough for pole, ending up 0.298s faster than Hamilton.
Isack Hadjar equalled his best career qualifying result with third but will start eighth due to a five-grid place penalty for a new internal combustion engine.
Championship leader Kimi Antonelli will start third after a costly mistake in Q2 forced him to use an extra set of tyres prior to Q3, leaving him with just one run in the final part of qualifying.

articles.title: Verstappen claims pole position for Bahrain GP in Malaysia
articles.summary: Four-time Formula One champion Max Verstappen was fastest on Saturday to claim pole position for the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia. It's a first pole position for the Red Bull driver since the Abu Dhabi GP in December 2025 as the Dutchman will bid to claim his first victory since that same race.
body: Verstappen clocked 1 minute 35.130 seconds, beating the Ferrari of Lewis Hamilton by 0.298 seconds. Third place also went to Red Bull with Isack Hadjar, who was 0.428 seconds behind his team-mate.
Championship leader Kimi Antonelli of Mercedes was fourth, while title holder Lando Norris clocked the sixth-best time.

F1 has returned to the Sepang International Circuit for the first time in nine years as the venue hosts the rearranged Bahrain GP, which was cancelled earlier this year due to the conflict in the Middle East.
Verstappen won the last race in Sepang in 2017, when the circuit hosted the Malaysian GP.

articles.title: Antonelli fastest from Verstappen ahead of qualifying in Malaysia
articles.summary: Kimi Antonelli was fastest from Max Verstappen in final practice for the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia to set up a Mercedes versus Red Bull fight for pole position.
body: Antonelli, who leads the Drivers' Championship by 66 points from his Mercedes team-mate George Russell, struggled on Friday but was 0.278s quicker than Verstappen.

Verstappen's Red Bull team-mate Isack Hadjar took third ahead of Russell fourth but both drivers were more than half a second behind Antonelli, who appears to have found a nice rhythm in time for qualifying later on Saturday at 9am, live on Sky Sports F1, at the Sepang International Circuit.
Mercedes have brought their biggest upgrade package since May's Canadian Grand Prix to Malaysia but Red Bull look set to be a threat again, just as they were last time out in Baku.
"Red Bull would have hoped to be closer to the Mercedes, but they are there or thereabouts once again," said Sky Sports F1's Anthony Davidson.

articles.title: Wade and Aspinall make statement ahead of World Grand Prix semi-finals
articles.summary: James Wade and Nathan Aspinall put in statement performances that will have made their semi-final opponents take note ahead of a mouthwatering Saturday night line-up at the World Grand Prix.
body: Aspinall threatened to set a new tournament record average when storming to a 3-0 win over Ryan Joyce, his 105.15 mark ultimately landing as the fourth-highest in history and the best-ever in a quarter-final.
Wade, meanwhile, dropped only one leg as he, in his words, "bashed up" world No 2 Gian van Veen in a match that lasted little more than 20 minutes.
"That really was a performance to remember from Wade," Sky Sports ' Wayne Mardle said. "From start to finish, he was absolutely devastating. World Class."
Three-time world champion John Part concurred with that assesment, saying: "James is not just looking like a great dart thrower to me, he's looking like a winner.
